did_you_know.text: The Hebrew word “tazria” comes from the root z-r-ʿ, meaning “seed”; the Torah uses an agricultural image to describe the beginning of life.
The eighth day became the established time for circumcision in Jewish tradition, even when it falls on Shabbat or a festival.
Allowing two birds instead of a lamb reflects an important social principle: even a poor family could take part in Temple rituals.
